title: Year 9 Science Test 1
topics: Variation and inheritance · Adaptation, extinction and natural selection · Cells and the microscope · Atoms and the periodic table
instructions: You have 40 minutes. Answer all the questions in Section A (30 marks), then try Section B (10 marks).
Write your answers in the spaces on this paper. If you need more space, use the back of the page and write the question number.
The marks for each part are shown in brackets, for example [2]. There are 40 marks in total.
Read each question carefully. Use the science key words in your answers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Put one tick in each row to show whether the factor is abiotic (non-living) or biotic (living).
parts.answer: temperature: abiotic; predation: biotic; amount of light: abiotic; infectious disease: biotic. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A scar is caused by a cut. Complete the sentence.
gaps: A scar is an example of ______________________ variation.
parts.answer: environmental

parts.label: c
parts.text: Put one tick in each row to show whether the variation is continuous or discontinuous.
parts.answer: height: continuous; blood group: discontinuous; hand span: continuous; tongue rolling: discontinuous. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the sentences using words from the box. Use each word once. One word is not needed.
gaps: Genetic information is stored in the ______________________ of a cell.
A sperm cell and an egg cell are both ______________________.
The new cell that is made is called a ______________________.
parts.answer: nucleus (1), gametes (1), fertilisation (1), zygote (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Tick the two characteristics that are inherited.
parts.answer: natural eye colour and blood group, both ticked and no others, for 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: What is an adaptation?
parts.answer: A characteristic (feature) that helps an organism survive in its habitat.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Draw one line from each way of protecting a species to how it works.

right: endangered animals are bred in captivity to increase their numbers
seeds, gametes or cells are stored at a low temperature
an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected

parts.answer: nature reserve: an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected (1); breeding programme: endangered animals are bred in captivity (1); gene bank: seeds, gametes or cells stored at a low temperature (1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Grey squirrels were brought to the UK from the USA. Red squirrels are now rare in most of the UK. Give one reason why grey squirrels have replaced red squirrels.
parts.answer: Any one of: greys can eat unripe acorns, so they eat the food before the reds do; greys store more body fat, so more survive the winter; greys carry squirrel pox, a disease that kills reds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: What causes inherited variation? Tick one box.
parts.answer: genes passed on from parents

parts.label: b
parts.text: In the 1800s, black peppered moths became more common near Manchester. The sentences below explain why, but they are in the wrong order. Write 1, 2, 3 and 4 in the boxes to put them in the correct order.

rows: Birds spotted and ate more pale moths than black moths.
A few moths had genes that made them black.
Each generation had more black moths than the one before.
Soot from factories made the tree trunks black.

parts.answer: Correct order: a few moths had genes that made them black (1); soot made the tree trunks black (2); birds ate more pale moths (3); each generation had more black moths (4). All four correct = 2 marks; first and last correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text: What is evolution?
parts.answer: A change over time in the characteristics of organisms (accept: a change in a species over many generations).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Which word means a scientific explanation that has been tested many times and is supported by a lot of evidence? Tick one box.
parts.answer: a theory

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows a plant cell. Write the name of each labelled part.
parts.answer: A cell wall (1), B nucleus (1), C chloroplast (1), D vacuole (1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: A microscope has a x10 eyepiece lens and a x4 objective lens. Calculate the total magnification.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table about the three particles in an atom. The first row has been done for you.
parts.answer: neutron: 0, in the nucleus; electron: -1, in shells around the nucleus. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23.

sub.text: How many protons does the atom have?
How many neutrons does the atom have?

parts.answer: (i) 11 protons (1). (ii) 23 - 11 = 12 neutrons (1).

parts.label: c
parts.text: A sodium atom has 11 electrons. Complete its electron configuration.
parts.answer: 2,8,1 (the missing number is 1).

sections.title: Section B: Stretch and Challenge
sections.intro: Try these when you have finished Section A. 10 marks. Stretch questions need a longer explanation. The Challenge question links ideas together.

questions.title: Natural selection in the Salton Sea

parts.label: a
parts.text: The Salton Sea in California has become saltier and saltier since 1905. Most fish species died out, but tilapia still live there and can cope with very salty water. Explain how natural selection made the tilapia able to live in very salty water.
parts.answer: By chance, some tilapia had genes (inherited variation) that helped them cope with salt (1). As the water got saltier, more of these fish survived and reproduced than the others (1), so they passed on their genes and each generation had more salt-tolerant fish, until all of them could cope (1). Do not credit 'the fish changed so they could cope'.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A microscope has a x10 eyepiece lens. A student uses the x40 objective lens and draws a cell that is 20 mm wide in the drawing.

sub.text: Calculate the actual width of the cell in millimetres. Show your working.

parts.answer: (i) 10 x 40 = x400 (1). (ii) actual size = image size / magnification = 20 / 400 (1) = 0.05 mm (1). Accept 50 micrometres.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Fluorine (atomic number 9) and chlorine (atomic number 17) are both in group 7 of the periodic table and react in similar ways.

sub.text: Write the electron configuration of a fluorine atom and of a chlorine atom.
Use your answer to explain why fluorine and chlorine react in similar ways.
Potassium has atomic number 19. Explain why potassium is in period 4.

parts.answer: (i) fluorine 2,7 (1); chlorine 2,8,7 (1). (ii) Both have seven electrons in the outer shell, and the outer electrons decide how an element reacts (1). (iii) Potassium is 2,8,8,1: its electrons fill four shells, and the period number is the number of shells (1).
